messages:
emily: Heads-up: change to release-freeze policy starting next month. We're moving away from a single weekly freeze to a rolling quiet-window model to better support global customers and reduce concentrated churn. Read below for the new flow and how exceptions work.

vince: big change. what's the reason?

emily: two reasons: (1) concentrated freezes were causing big morning spikes when they ended, and (2) global teams needed more flexibility. Rolling windows let us stagger brief quiet periods per-region.

tara: how will this affect our release train cadence practically?

emily: main points:
- default: 2x 3-hour quiet windows per week, per-region (teams can opt-in/out)
- quiet window goal: minimal high-risk infra changes (kernel, runtime, major model swaps)
- low-risk config/feature flips still allowed with preflight + owner signoff
- exceptions: owners submit via `releasectl exception create` with a short risk statement

vince: can you show the exact exception command so automated checks can run?

emily: sure. Example:
```
releasectl exception create --name ranking-rollout --owner @vince --reason \"partner demo\" --impact low --tests smoke,perf
```
The system will run automated preflight checks and mark it pending. Ops/oncall review if kernel-level libs are touched.

ops-bot: NEW PRE-FLIGHT CHECKS (automated):
- infra health check
- db replica lag < 300ms
- canary baseline comparison
- alerting hooks configured
- model-cache warm-up verified
If any check fails, exception is auto-rejected.

vince: what's the approval SLA for exceptions? We sometimes need last-minute sign-off.

emily: target: 4h for standard exceptions during business hours, 30m for emergency (escalate to @oncall). After hours, auto-grant only for kernel-free low-risk requests if preflight passes.

tara: will the Console show region-specific quiet windows?

emily: yes. We'll add region banners and a per-team calendar. Console banner example: \"Rolling quiet window: eu-west Tue 02:00-05:00 UTC. See release dashboard for exceptions.\"

ops-bot: Automation commands we'll use during a quiet window:
- tilt routing: `routingctl tilt --to eu-west-quiet --percent 60 --duration 3h`
- provision helper nodes: `infractl provision --zone eu-west-1 --type gpu-small --count 2 --ttl 4h`

vince: fallback policies?
emily: unchanged: if error-rate > 1% or p95 latency jumps > 50% we trigger fallback. Example policy in the system: `fallback: reroute->stable, pause-rollouts, notify->#incidents`

deploy-bot: We've created templates: `releasectl exception template --id rolling-quiet-v1`. Scheduled jobs for pilot rollout banners will be created next week.

oncall: Oncall note: during pilot week we'll post 10-min cadence updates in this thread for visibility. Escalate immediately if you see regressions.

emily: Pilot plan: next week we'll run the rolling model in beta for eu-west and us-west. Teams: opt-in via the release dashboard by EOD Friday. We'll reassess after the pilot and update docs.

vince: thanks. We'll opt the embeddings and ranking teams in.

emily: great. Final: if you need an exception for the pilot, run the command and tag @oncall. I'll post the console banner copy and the new runbook link shortly. :rocket:
